page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor operating at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 32 dedicated virtual CPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 8.0 GB RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs installed, and the virtual machine provides 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth alongside zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Because this configuration includes no local storage, all persistent disks and operating system partitions must be provisioned via remote network-attached volumes. Network-attached storage shares the 16 Gbps network interface with application communication. The generous memory footprint relative to core count delivers cost efficiency for architectures limited by memory capacity rather than compute throughput, minimizing excessive vCPU licensing overhead while satisfying substantial RAM demands.

The hardware specification makes ecs.r9a.8xlarge suited for memory-intensive workloads that execute largely within RAM. Typical deployments include in-memory databases, Redis or Memcached distributed caching layers, real-time stream analytics, and enterprise application servers running large JVM heaps.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, offering an expansive 8.0 GB per-core memory ratio. Built on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T25 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz via KVM virtualization, it is engineered for operations requiring significant memory residency. The server includes no local disk storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage solutions, and features a baseline network throughput of 16 Gbps. It contains no GPU accelerators. The 1:8 compute-to-memory balance offers economical resource utilization for systems that demand high memory capacity without the necessity of over-provisioning computational cores. The ecs.r9a.8xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, caching services, business intelligence processing, and large-scale enterprise backend systems.
